amb_user_query: For each author, show their name and how many of their books are bestsellers. Put the authors with the most first.
query: For each author with at least one book that sold 10 or more copies in total, count those books. Show the author's name and the count, highest count first.

non_critical_ambiguity.sql_snippet: JOIN authors a ON t.author_id = a.author_id

sol_sql: SELECT a.name, COUNT(*) AS bestsellers FROM authors a JOIN (SELECT b.author_id FROM books b JOIN sales s ON s.book_id = b.book_id GROUP BY b.book_id HAVING SUM(s.quantity) >= 10) t ON t.author_id = a.author_id GROUP BY a.author_id ORDER BY bestsellers DESC

amb_user_query: What is the typical discount in each genre?
query: For each genre, give the average discount rate over its sales, where the discount rate of a sale is 1 - unit_price / list_price.
sol_sql: SELECT b.genre, AVG(1 - s.unit_price / b.list_price) AS avg_discount FROM sales s JOIN books b ON b.book_id = s.book_id GROUP BY b.genre

amb_user_query: Show the title and revenue of each recent release.
query: For each book published in 2022 or later, show its title and its revenue, the sum of quantity * unit_price over its sales.
sol_sql: SELECT b.title, SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS revenue FROM books b JOIN sales s ON s.book_id = b.book_id WHERE b.published_year >= 2022 GROUP BY b.book_id

follow_up.query: Now keep only the ones that brought in more than 150 dollars.
sol_sql: SELECT b.title, SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) AS revenue FROM books b JOIN sales s ON s.book_id = b.book_id WHERE b.published_year >= 2022 GROUP BY b.book_id HAVING SUM(s.quantity * s.unit_price) > 150
